name: Noble
body:
A sword may kill, but a word may save. Without even drawing a weapon, a Noble is as powerful as a master swordsman. Nobles exemplify the arts of diplomacy, bluffing, misdirection, compromise, and intimidation. Artists paint, but nobles talk. Nobles develop a near perfect understanding of charm and rhetoric that allows them to walk into almost any room and control it with their bearing. On the other hand, nobles have enough wit to know when a little white lie could work in their favor. Many nobles are poised princesses who have worked their way through charm school and made themselves into walking works of art. Some are ruthless crime-lords or even Charismatic commanders. Wherever they come from and wherever they are, a noble normally has the complete control of any situation through sheer force of personality.

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The noble’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (all) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Stealth (Dex)

Skill Points Per Level: 4 + Int modifier

Class Features

The following are the class features of the noble.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A noble is proficient in the use of all simple weapons and with light armor.

Wealth

Each time a noble gains a level, she gains an amount of gold depending on her noble level as indicated below from her patron(s). This money is delivered to her in a manner that she designates (Placed in a bank, delivered in person, etc). It is delivered in a timely fashion, though not instantly. The money’s use is up to the noble. If she is out of reach or out of contact with her patron (such as being on another plane), the funds will be made available to her when she is able to be reached again. A GM may adjust the amount gained per level depending on the campaign.

Patron

Your character’s patron is anyone connected to you with a significant wealth they are willing to impart to you on a regular basis. This might be your family (if they are wealthy), a crime syndicate, a sugar daddy, a blackmailed government official, a paycheck from an organization you are deeply affiliated with, a banking cartel, or even an otherworldly being. This is an excellent opportunity for your GM to weave your character into the story. It can make for interesting plot hooks and roleplaying opportunities. A noble disowned by his patron may not continue to take levels in the noble class until they find a new patron (or make amends with their old one).

Talk Down (Ex)

At 1st level, a noble knows how to defuse a situation. As a standard action, she may make a Diplomacy check against an opponent within 60 ft. This is not considered an attack action, it is considered a Diplomacy check. If the check is successful, the opponent takes 1d6 + Charisma modifier in morale damage (see the “morale damage” section following the class features). This damage increases by 1d6 at every odd level after 1st.

The DC of this check is equal to 15 + the target’s Hit Dice + the target’s Wisdom modifier. The creature must share a language with the noble (or be able to communicate with them in another fashion) in order to be affected by this ability. This provokes an attack of opportunity.

Social Bonus Feat

At 2nd-level and every even level thereafter, a noble gains a bonus feat from the following list: Alertness, Childlike*, Cosmopolitan*, Charlatan**, Deceitful, Dashing Scoundrel**, Enforcer*, Expert Linguist**, Femme Fatale**, Lady Killer**, Leadership, Preacher, Public Speaker**, Stealthy, Skill Focus (any noble class skill), Sociable*, Stone?Faced*, Taunt*, or Vixen**.

The noble must meet the prerequisites of the selected bonus feats.

Teamwork Feat

At 3rd-level and every odd level thereafter, a noble gains a bonus feat. This feat must be listed as a teamwork feat.

Cutting Words (Ex)

Sometimes words sting more than a blade. It doesn’t hurt to include the blade, however. A noble of 3rd level or higher can cause a stinging wound to hurt even more with a sour word. Targets that are successfully intimidated by the noble take additional damage from allies’ attacks. This morale bonus to damage is equal to 1/2 the noble’s Charisma modifier. An ally may only apply this once per round to each intimidated creature it attacks.

Commanding Persona (Ex)

At 4th-level, a noble can grant any one of her teamwork feats to all allies within 30 feet who can see and hear her as a swift action. Allies retain the use of this bonus feat for 3 rounds plus 1 round for every 2 levels the noble possesses. The noble can use this ability once per day at 4th-level, plus one additional time per day at 9thlevel and every 5 levels thereafter.

Silver Tongue (Ex)

A 5th-level noble can make quick work of any social situation with a quick word. She may make Diplomacy or Intimidate checks to change an opponent’s attitude towards her in combat as a full action, instead of taking 1 minute to do so. She may do this a number of times per day equal to 1/2 her Charisma modifier (minimum 1). The normal rules for Diplomacy checks apply (Such as the inability to affect the same creatures twice in a 24 hour period).

Soothe the Savage Beast (Ex)

At 6th-level, a noble can take a standard action to make a Diplomacy check against a creature to attempt to calm them. The DC of this check is equal to 15 + the target’s Hit Dice + the target’s Wisdom modifier. A successful check means the creature is subject to a mundane effect similar to the calm emotions spell cast by a spellcaster of equal level to the noble. This is a mind-affecting ability and the creature must share a language with the noble. Additionally, a noble may not use this ability on a creature of 3 or less Intelligence.

Words Like Knives (Ex)

The venomous words that slip from the lips of a noble can sink deep enough to demoralize a target to the point where they are unable to fight. At 7th level, when using the cutting words class feature, if the noble exceeds the DC required to Intimidate a creature by at least 5, the target also takes a -2 penalty to AC until the end of its next turn.

Playing a Noble

A noble’s main focus should be on his Charisma when selecting his ability scores. A high Constitution never hurts as they have d8 Hit Dice. Their real focus needs to be on the allocation of their skill points. Diplomacy and Intimidate are key skills for them as many of their class features function off of them. These can get quite high due to the noble’s social bonus feats and should be the main focus on the character’s skill point allocation. Other Charisma based skills that interact with social aspects of the game (Bluff and Sense Motive) should also be high in priority. Linguistics is a very useful skill, as the more languages you know, the more types of creatures you can affect with your talk down class feature.

A noble should have the social aspects of the game on lockdown, freeing them up to take a secondary specialty. Investing the feats to get them up to wearing heavy armor and a shield can make them quite the powerhouse as they are not required to wield anything while using their talk down class feature (coupling this with something like the Broken Wing Gambit teamwork feat is a nice mix!). Alternatively, taking the teamwork approach allows you to become something of a battlefield commander. Later levels gives you access to more teamwork feats and you can share them with your allies via the commanding persona class feature. This has turned the tide in more than one battle.

A noble spends most combat rounds either sharing their teamwork feats or using talk down. Despite the perception of a noble character in different forms of media as taking a backseat during battle, this class has a way of dealing a respectable amount of damage. Your talk down deals 1d6 per 2 levels of noble you have and most of the time you are going to be able to effect a creature with that class feature. This makes you a reliable source of damage. Keep in mind that morale damage is a different type of damage (similar to non-lethal damage) and when healed it is restored along side the other kinds of damage the creature has taken (So if a creature is healed 20 hp the creature restores 20 morale damage, 20 normal damage, and 20 non-lethal damage if they have it).

Another aspect of the noble you need to consider is their increased wealth. While a shiny new suit of +3 full plate looks nice, consider what else your money can be used for. Bribes (even very large ones) can help out of a bad situation and hiring help can allow your party to circumvent obstacles. Couple that with your formidable Diplomacy score and making friends wherever you go shouldn’t be a problem.

When it comes to using the talk down class feature, you need to remember that this has to make sense. A noble is not a class for those you do not like to roleplay. Each time you use it, you need to make a legitimate case for that morale damage to your GM. By the sixth straight hour of a game sometimes you might feel tempted to just roll the dice and mutter some vague insult. That doesn’t cut it. You need to be pushing your mind to come up with ways to gain this advantage. Depending on your character’s background good fallbacks include: reminders of your target’s impending doom due to their poor performance in past rounds, legitimate offers of compassion or heartfelt pleads for peace (careful not be holding a bloody sword while doing this), bribery, or a commanding order to cease the senseless bloodshed. A GM with a noble in their game needs to be vigilant about this. Talk down requires a Diplomacy check, while success may have its benefits beyond just morale damage. If an offer the noble makes strikes a cord with an enemy, play that up; offering 14,000 gp to a pirate crew to turn on their dishonest captain might not be such a bad deal.

As a noble remember: roleplay everything, influence anyone you can, be smart, and keep the Charisma score high!
